sentences: I unfold the paper map and check the scale bar at the bottom to estimate the distance between two towns.
I trace the blue line representing the river to see where it crosses the main road.
I look for the compass rose in the corner to confirm which direction is north before I start walking.
I measure the distance between two points using a ruler and the map's scale.
I check the legend to find out what the small triangle symbol means.
I locate the contour lines that show the steepness of the hill near the trailhead.
I scan the index at the back of the atlas to find the page number for a specific city.
I fold the map along its original creases so it fits back into the glove compartment.
I enter the coordinates into my handheld GPS unit and wait for it to acquire a signal.
I compare the road map with the topographic map to see which one shows the hiking trails.
I trace the boundary line between the two counties with my finger.
I note the grid lines and their numbers to pinpoint the location of the lake.
I look at the inset map in the corner that shows the downtown area in more detail.
I check the map's copyright date to see how recently it was updated.
I identify the different colors used to represent elevation ranges on the physical map.
I follow the dotted line that marks the ferry route across the bay.
I use the map's alphabetical list of street names to find the intersection.
I rotate the map so that the direction I am facing aligns with the map's orientation.
I mark a small X on the map to remember the location of the campsite.
I read the latitude and longitude numbers along the edges of the map.
